content: Phosphatidylinositol-glycan-specific phospholipase D is an enzyme encoded by the GPLD1 gene in humans. Numerous proteins are attached to the extracellular surface of eukaryotic plasma membranes via a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor. This GPI anchor is a glycolipid structure present on various blood cells. The protein produced by the GPLD1 gene functions as an enzyme that degrades GPI anchors. Specifically, glycosylphosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase D1 catalyzes the hydrolysis of the inositol phosphate bond in proteins that are anchored to the membrane by phosphatidylinositol glycans. This enzymatic activity results in the release of the anchored protein from the plasma membrane. Additionally, GPLD1 has been demonstrated to interact with Apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) and Apolipoprotein A4 (ApoA4).
